Bug_Details: Using an unnecessarily-wide comparison method can lead to lossy comparison Implicit widening conversions when comparing two primitives with methods like Float.compare can lead to lossy comparison. For example, Float.compare(Integer.MAX_VALUE, Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1) == 0. Use a compare method with non-lossy conversion, or ideally no conversion if possible.
Bug_Explanation: The code uses Float.compare to compare two integer values. This leads to an implicit widening conversion which can cause a loss of precision, resulting in incorrect comparison results.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case testShowBugWithMaxInt triggers the bug by using the Float.compare method to compare two integer values which are close to each other in value, specifically Integer.MAX_VALUE and Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1. This results in a loss of precision due to implicit widening conversion, causing the comparison to incorrectly evaluate as equal (0), which is not expected.
